message.content:
Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell, generating ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. The number of mitochondria per cell can vary widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands:

| Cell Type | Typical Mitochondrial Count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Red blood cells** (which lack mitochondria) | 0 |
| **Neurons** (high energy demand) | ~10 000–30 000 |
| **Skeletal muscle cells** | ~5 000–10 000 |
| **Liver hepatocytes** | ~1 000–2 000 |
| **Epithelial cells** | ~200–500 |
| **Stem cells** | ~50–200 |

These numbers are approximate averages; actual counts can differ based on species, developmental stage, and physiological conditions. In general, most mammalian cells contain between a few hundred and several thousand mitochondria, with highly active cells like neurons and muscle fibers having the highest densities.
